repeat.title: Campus orientation
sentences: Welcome to the student center.
The information desk is on your left.
You can pick up your ID card here today.
The dining hall is open until nine on weekdays.
Please remember to bring a photo when you register for parking.
If you have any questions about housing, the office is on the second floor.
Free guided tours of the campus leave from the main entrance every hour until four.

repeat.title: Science museum
sentences: Our next tour starts in five minutes.
Please stay with the group at all times.
This gallery shows how volcanoes are formed.
Photography is allowed, but please don't use a flash.
The model on your right was built by students from the local university.
After the tour, you're welcome to visit the planetarium on the lower level.
Tickets for the evening show can be purchased at the front desk until six o'clock.

repeat.title: Library orientation
sentences: The library opens at eight every morning.
Quiet study areas are on the third floor.
You can borrow up to twenty books at a time.
Laptops are available for loan at the front desk.
Please return all items on time to avoid late fees.
Group study rooms can be reserved online for up to three hours.
If you need help finding sources for your research, ask a librarian at the reference desk.

repeat.title: Residence hall meeting
sentences: Welcome to your new residence hall.
Quiet hours begin at ten on weeknights.
Laundry machines are located in the basement.
Please keep your door locked when you leave the room.
Visitors must sign in at the front desk after nine p.m.
If something in your room is broken, submit a repair request online.
Our first floor meeting will be held in the common room on Thursday evening at seven.

repeat.title: Biology lab instructions
sentences: Today we'll look at plant cells.
Each pair will share one microscope.
Place a thin slice of onion on the slide.
Add a single drop of stain before covering the sample.
Start with the lowest magnification and focus slowly.
Draw what you observe and label the cell wall and the nucleus.
When you have finished, clean your slides and return all equipment to the cabinet by the window.

repeat.title: City bus tour
sentences: Good morning and welcome aboard.
Our tour will last about two hours.
On your left is the oldest bridge in the city.
We'll stop at the history museum for forty minutes.
Please make sure you are back on the bus by eleven.
The market across the street is famous for its fresh seafood and local crafts.
Before we finish, we'll drive past the university, which was founded more than two hundred years ago.

interview.intro: Thank you for taking part in our research project. We're interested in how students use technology for learning. I'm going to ask you a few questions.
questions: First, could you tell me about a digital tool or app that you use often for studying?
Some people say that studying with a smartphone nearby makes it harder to concentrate. What has your experience been?
If you were advising a new student, would you recommend taking notes by hand or on a laptop? Why?
Finally, some universities are considering banning devices in lecture halls. Do you think that's a good idea? Please explain.
tips: 最初の1文で質問に直接答える（I mostly use...）
理由を1つ、具体例を1つ加える
後半2問は意見問題：立場→理由→例→簡単なまとめ
沈黙を避けるつなぎ表現：That's an interesting question. / Let me think...
45秒で約90〜120語が目安

interview.intro: Hello, and thanks for joining us. We're conducting a study about how people experience life in cities. I'd like to ask you four questions.
questions: To begin, what do you like most about the place where you live now?
Tell me about a time when you had to adjust to living in a new environment.
Many young people move to large cities for work. Do you think this trend is good for smaller towns? Why or why not?
Last question. If your city could make one change to improve residents' quality of life, what should it be, and why?
tips: 最初の1文で質問に直接答える
経験を問う質問は「いつ・どこで・何が・どう感じたか」の順で話す
意見問題は利点と欠点の両面に触れると深みが出る
沈黙を避けるつなぎ表現：That's an interesting question. / Let me think...
45秒で約90〜120語が目安

interview.intro: Thanks for participating in our study on how people learn new skills. I'd like to ask you some questions about your experiences.
questions: To start, what is a skill you learned recently, and how did you learn it?
Do you prefer studying alone or with other people? Why?
Some people believe that failure is an important part of learning. Do you agree? Please give an example.
Finally, should schools spend more time teaching practical life skills, such as managing money? Why or why not?
tips: 最初の1文で質問に直接答える
経験を問う質問は「いつ・どこで・何を・どうなったか」の順で話す
意見問題は立場→理由→例→まとめ
45秒で約90〜120語が目安

interview.intro: Hello, and thank you for joining us. We're researching students' daily habits and their effect on well-being. I'll ask you four questions.
questions: First, could you describe a typical morning on a school or work day?
What do you usually do to relieve stress?
Many people find it difficult to maintain a regular exercise routine. What do you think makes it difficult, and how can people overcome it?
Last question. Should universities be responsible for students' physical and mental health? Please explain your view.
tips: 日常の描写は時系列（First, Then, After that）で整理する
理由を述べたら具体的な行動例を加える
「どう克服するか」には具体策を1〜2個挙げる
45秒で約90〜120語が目安

interview.intro: Thank you for taking the time to talk with us. Our research focuses on how young people think about their future careers.
questions: To begin, what kind of job would you like to have in ten years?
Tell me about a person who has influenced your career plans.
Some people choose jobs that pay well, while others choose jobs they enjoy. Which is more important to you, and why?
Finally, how do you think technology like AI will change the job market in the future?
tips: 将来の話は would like to / I hope to / I'm planning to を使い分ける
人物について話すときは「誰か→何をしたか→自分への影響」の順
二択の質問は一方を選び、もう一方の価値にも一言触れる
45秒で約90〜120語が目安

interview.intro: Hi, thanks for joining our project. We're interested in how people's everyday choices relate to the environment.
questions: First, what is one thing you do in your daily life that is good for the environment?
Have you ever changed a habit for environmental reasons? Please describe what happened.
Some people say individual actions make little difference compared with government policies. What do you think?
Last question. If you could introduce one environmental rule in your city, what would it be and why?
tips: 身近な具体例（交通手段・買い物・食事）を用意しておく
過去の経験は過去形で一貫させる
仮定の質問には If I could..., I would... で答える
45秒で約90〜120語が目安
